text:
mira: hey folks — first day question. I ran `aws sso login --profile redwood-onboard` then `aws eks update-kubeconfig --name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-onboard` but `kubectl get pods -n mira-dev` returns Forbidden. `kubectl config get-contexts` shows two contexts (one arn and one named dev-team). Any quick tips?

devops: welcome! most likely your SSO principal isn't bound to a RoleBinding in mira-dev yet. Two options: file the k8s access form or we can issue a short-lived ServiceAccount kubeconfig so you can iterate immediately.

mira: where's the form? also what's involved with the SA kubeconfig?

lia: https://redwood.example.com/access -> choose "Kubernetes namespace access" and request `namespace=mira-dev`, role `onboard-edit`. For the SA flow, DM @devops with your ticket id and reason; we create a namespaced SA, export the secret, and give you a kubeconfig that points to the cluster with that token. It's temporary (4h) and locked to the namespace.

devops: if you want to paste the exec block from `kubectl config view --raw` (the `users:` section) we can confirm it's SSO. But yeah SA kubeconfig looks like this sketch: ```apiVersion: v1
clusters:
- cluster:
    server: https://ABC.eks.redwood.internal
    certificate-authority-data: <redacted>
  name: redwood-dev
users:
- name: sa-mira
  user:
    token: <redacted-token>
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: redwood-dev
    user: sa-mira
    namespace: mira-dev
  name: sa-mira@mira-dev
current-context: sa-mira@mira-dev```

devops: once we upload it you'll do `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/mira-sa get pods -n mira-dev`. Reminder: do NOT check that file into git or paste the token publicly.

infra-bot: access request created by mira at 1999991240  id K-20456. Assigned to infra. ETA ~1h.

mira: filed the form and DMed @devops. thanks! update: devops uploaded the SA kubeconfig to my ticket, ran `kubectl --kubeconfig=~/.kube/mira-sa get pods -n mira-dev` and it works. They also left a note: once infra approves the preferred flow is SSO role mapping, so re-run `aws sso login` afterwards to pick up the RoleBinding. Good to go. :party_parrot:
